work_rules.authority: Labor Code of the Philippines (P.D. 442, as amended) Book III: art.82 (coverage), art.83 (eight-hour day), art.85 (meal period), art.86 (night shift differential), art.87 (overtime), art.91 (weekly rest day), art.93 (rest-day premium) and art.94 (holiday pay), with Proclamation No. 1006, s.2025 for the 2026 regular holidays and special (non-working) days. Applied 2026-09-18 (2): art.86 and Handbook ch.5: the night shift differential is 10% of the hour’s own rate, so 13 on a rest day or a special day, 20 on a regular holiday, 26 on a regular holiday falling on the rest day, 15 on a special day on the rest day, and on the overtime hours of each 12.5, 16.9, 26, 33.8 and 19.5 (`night_premium` adds as expressions over the day; the first eight night hours of a rest day or holiday are its ordinary ones). Handbook ch.2 §D–E: a monthly-paid employee — one "paid every day of the month, including unworked rest days, special days, and regular holidays", declared on the contract as `terms.paid_rest_days` (applied 2026-09-23, round 4: the payroll group is the employer’s own label and states no law) — is prorated and has an absence deducted on the 365 factor, 30.4167 a month (`proration_by`); the daily-paid keep 21.75 or 26.0833. Applied 2026-09-19 (2): The night-differential ladder reads the day type (`day_type`, which the holiday takes under `holiday_rest_precedence: PUBLIC_HOLIDAY`); `holiday.kind` is the published row’s kind (PUBLIC | SPECIAL | SUBSTITUTE), and a day-type literal against it never matched. Applied 2026-09-23 (PH audit): Handbook ch.2 §D, ch.3 §C, ch.4 §D state each day's pay as a total — a regular holiday worked 200%, a special day 130%, a rest day 130%, a regular holiday on the rest day 260%, a special day on the rest day 150%. The salary (261, 313 and 365 factors alike) and the daily-paid roster already pay a working holiday at 100%, so its first eight hours add the rest: 100% and 30% (`OT-2.0X`, `OT-1.3X`). The 365 factor (`terms.paid_rest_days`) also pays the rest day in the salary, so on it the rest-day rows add 30%, 160% and 50%; every other employee's rest day is unpaid and the rows carry the whole 130%, 260% and 150%. Hours beyond eight are paid by no base and keep their whole 169%, 260%, 338% and 195%. Applied 2026-09-23 (round 2): DOLE Handbook (2022) ch.2 §C: where two regular holidays fall on one day (a `DOUBLE_HOLIDAY` calendar row), the day is at least 200% of the daily wage unworked (`DOUBLE-HOLIDAY-UNWORKED`: a second day’s wage) and 300% worked (`OT-3.0X`: two more days on top of the day the wage pays); the guide computations (ch.4 §D) give 390% on a rest day (`OT-3.9X-REST`, 290% for the 365-factor employee, `terms.paid_rest_days`, whose salary pays the rest day), overtime 3 × 1.3 = 390% (`OT-3.9X`) and 3.9 × 1.3 = 507% on a rest day (`OT-5.07X-REST`), and night shift 10% of those rates (30, 39; overtime 39, 50.7). Ch.2 §D–E: an unworked regular holiday is paid only to an employee present, or on leave with pay, on the workday immediately preceding it (a rest or non-work day looks back further; two successive holidays pass the test through the first); `payroll.regular_holiday_prior_workday` applies it to the daily-paid wage and `holiday.prior_day_present` to the double holiday’s second day.

wages.authority: Applied 2026-09-18 (2): the wage orders state a daily rate; `by_region` carries it × 313/12 and `wages.scale` restates the floor on the person’s own factor — 365/12 for the monthly-paid, 261/12 on a five-day week, 313/12 on a six-day one — and the apprentice’s 75% (RA 6727; Labor Code arts.61, 75). Applied 2026-09-19 (3): Wage Order No. IVA-22 (effective 5 Oct 2025; nwpc.dole.gov.ph/region-iva): non-agriculture ₱600 in the Extended Metropolitan Area and the component cities (`IV-A`), ₱550 in 1st-class municipalities, ₱510 in reclassified 1st-class and 2nd–5th-class municipalities, the last two stepping to ₱550 and ₱525 on 1 April 2026 — the version from that date carries the second tranche. Each figure is the daily rate × 313 ÷ 12. Applied 2026-09-23 (audit): sector floors beside the area ones, for an establishment whose `company.region` names its sector — `NCR-AGRI-SMALL` is NCR agriculture, service/retail of 15 workers or fewer and manufacturing under 10 (₱658 under NCR-26, ₱718 under NCR-28; nwpc.dole.gov.ph/ncr/); `IV-A-RETAIL-SMALL` is IV-A retail/service of 10 workers or fewer (₱485 under IVA-22 from 5 Oct 2025, ₱508 from 1 Apr 2026; nwpc.dole.gov.ph/region-iva/). Each × 313 ÷ 12. The RA 9504 minimum-wage-earner test reads the same floor, so an employee of such an establishment above the sector floor is withheld on. Applied 2026-09-23 (round 2): RA 10361 (Batas Kasambahay) s.24: a domestic worker’s floor is the regional board’s domestic-worker wage order, a monthly figure, never the establishment order — `by_employment_type.DOMESTIC`, held on its own (scale 1). NCR only, from the wage orders themselves: NCR-DW-05 ₱7,000 a month from 4 January 2025, and NCR-DW-06 (approved 15 January 2026, published 22 January, effective 7 February 2026; nwpc.dole.gov.ph/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/Wage-Order-No.-NCR-DW-06.pdf) ₱7,800 — this version states ₱7,000. Other regions’ domestic orders are not transcribed.

encashment.authority: DOLE Handbook on Workers Statutory Monetary Benefits, Service Incentive Leave, Conversion: salary rate on the conversion date, with pro-rata conversion. A daily contract supplies its daily salary; an hourly contract uses its normal scheduled hours per workday. Monthly equivalent factors follow paid-day coverage. Standing allowances require express basic-salary classification. https://nwpc.dole.gov.ph/wp-content/uploads/2023/08/2023-07-25-Handbook-on-Workers-Statutory-Monetary-Benefits-2023_edition.pdf Applied 2026-09-23 (round 5): a weekly contract converts at the same salary rate on the conversion date — its week's wage over the days that wage pays: the working days of the week, or all seven where the contract pays the rest day too (the Handbook's monthly-paid/daily-paid distinction, Rules on EEMR factors 365 and 313/261, applied to a week).

sources.instructions:
Sources are the primary instrument first — the statute or regulation in the national law database, the gazette, or the table the authority itself publishes — one page per fact the version seals, never a news article or a commentary. A historical version lists the instruments in force on its own effective date. Where the primary host refuses the reader (sso.agc.gov.sg, officialgazette.gov.ph, peraturan.bpk.go.id, kwsp.gov.my, hrdcorp.gov.my answer 403 to Norbital-Public-Page-Reader) the authority’s own published table is listed instead, or the Wayback Machine’s dated copy of the authority’s own page or PDF (web.archive.org/web/<timestamp>id_/<url>) — never a host the reader cannot open.
officialgazette.gov.ph — the Official Gazette: Republic Acts, proclamations, executive orders. A proclamation is /<yyyy>/<mm>/<dd>/proclamation-no-<n>-s-<year>/ (HTML, full text); /section/proclamations/ lists the newest first; /nationwide-holidays/<year>/ is the holiday calendar. lawphil.net mirrors the same texts and is corroboration only.
sss.gov.ph — /pay-contribution/ carries the contribution schedule (the 2025 table PDF under /wp-content/uploads/ is 6.3 MB, over the reader limit: read the HTML page); /sss-circulars/ lists circulars by year.
philhealth.gov.ph — /advisories/<year>/ lists advisories; each is /advisories/<year>/PA<year>-<nnnn>.pdf (small, text). /partners/employers/ContributionTable_v2.pdf is the premium table.
pagibigfund.gov.ph — Circular 460 at /document/pdf/circulars/provident/Circular No. 460 - Guidelines on the Pag-IBIG Fund… (1.9 MB, text): the 1%/2% tiers and the ₱10,000 fund salary cap.
bir.gov.ph — bir-cdn.bir.gov.ph/local/pdf/Annex E RR 11-2018.pdf is the withholding table (monthly and semi-monthly columns, 0.3 MB); revenue regulation digests are under bir-cdn.bir.gov.ph/BIR/pdf/.
nwpc.dole.gov.ph — regional wage orders: /ncr/, /region-iva/ (and the other regions); /bwc-handbook-workers-statutory-monetary-benefits/ is the DOLE Handbook (factors, premiums, 13th month).
pco.gov.ph answers 403 to the reader; use the Gazette.

Finding changes (read these before comparing, every run):
Wage orders: read https://nwpc.dole.gov.ph/feed/ (RSS) for new RTWPB orders, then open https://nwpc.dole.gov.ph/statistics/summary-of-latest-wage-orders-issued-by-the-regional-boards/ and follow its 'Download PDF' (Latest-Wage-Order-Matrix-<date>.pdf, a text PDF with issue/publication/effectivity per region). Effectivity is 15 days after publication when the matrix leaves it blank. The regional pages (/ncr/, /region-iva/ …) link the signed wage-order PDFs. These are scans with no text layer, so take the figures from the matrix. SSS: newest CI number on /sss-circulars/, and the rate table on /pay-contribution/. PhilHealth: /advisories/<YYYY>/ and /circulars/<YYYY>/; premium changes are 'Premium Contribution … for CY<YYYY>' advisories. BIR: every www.bir.gov.ph listing (RR, RMC, WithHoldingTax) is a client-rendered shell ('Loading…'), so it cannot be read. Discover RR/RMC numbers from a big-4 alert list (PwC PH Tax Alerts, SGV/EY Tax Bulletin), then open the PDF at https://bir-cdn.bir.gov.ph/BIR/pdf/RR%20No.%20<n>-<yyyy>.pdf. Holidays: lawphil proclamation index for discovery only (officialgazette.gov.ph returns 403). Pag-IBIG and DOLE/BWC labor advisories are bot-walled: use news only to discover, and do not cite them.

A count of the establishment, with no statutory default: required.

name: Philippines
change_summary: No change of law. work_rules.authority: Labor Code of the Philippines (P.D. 442, as amended) Book III: art.82 (coverage), art.83 (eight-hour day), art.85 (meal period), art.86 (night shift differential), art.87 (overtime), art.91 (weekly rest day), art.93 (rest-day premium) and art.94 (holiday pay), with Proclamation No. 1006, s.2025 for the 2026 regular holidays and special (non-working) days. Applied 2026-09-18 (2): art.86 and Handbook ch.5: the night shift differential is 10% of the hour’s own rate, so 13 on a rest day or a special day, 20 on a regular holiday, 26 on a regular holiday falling on the rest day, 15 on a special day on the rest day, and on the overtime hours of each 12.5, 16.9, 26, 33.8 and 19.5 (`night_premium` adds as expressions over the day; the first eight night hours of a rest day or holiday are its ordinary ones). Handbook ch.2 §D–E: a monthly-paid employee — one "paid every day of the month, including unworked rest days, special days, and regular holidays", declared on the contract as `terms.paid_rest_days` (applied 2026-09-23, round 4: the payroll group is the employer’s own label and states no law) — is prorated and has an absence deducted on the 365 factor, 30.4167 a month (`proration_by`); the daily-paid keep 21.75 or 26.0833. Applied 2026-09-19 (2): The night-differential ladder reads the day type (`day_type`, which the holiday takes under `holiday_rest_precedence: PUBLIC_HOLIDAY`); `holiday.kind` is the published row’s kind (PUBLIC | SPECIAL | SUBSTITUTE), and a day-type literal against it never matched. Applied 2026-09-23 (PH audit): Handbook ch.2 §D, ch.3 §C, ch.4 §D state each day's pay as a total — a regular holiday worked 200%, a special day 130%, a rest day 130%, a regular holiday on the rest day 260%, a special day on the rest day 150%. The salary (261, 313 and 365 factors alike) and the daily-paid roster already pay a working holiday at 100%, so its first eight hours add the rest: 100% and 30% (`OT-2.0X`, `OT-1.3X`). The 365 factor (`terms.paid_rest_days`) also pays the rest day in the salary, so on it the rest-day rows add 30%, 160% and 50%; every other employee's rest day is unpaid and the rows carry the whole 130%, 260% and 150%. Hours beyond eight are paid by no base and keep their whole 169%, 260%, 338% and 195%. Applied 2026-09-23 (round 2): DOLE Handbook (2022) ch.2 §C: where two regular holidays fall on one day (a `DOUBLE_HOLIDAY` calendar row), the day is at least 200% of the daily wage unworked (`DOUBLE-HOLIDAY-UNWORKED`: a second day’s wage) and 300% worked (`OT-3.0X`: two more days on top of the day the wage pays); the guide computations (ch.4 §D) give 390% on a rest day (`OT-3.9X-REST`, 290% for the 365-factor employee, `terms.paid_rest_days`, whose salary pays the rest day), overtime 3 × 1.3 = 390% (`OT-3.9X`) and 3.9 × 1.3 = 507% on a rest day (`OT-5.07X-REST`), and night shift 10% of those rates (30, 39; overtime 39, 50.7). Ch.2 §D–E: an unworked regular holiday is paid only to an employee present, or on leave with pay, on the workday immediately preceding it (a rest or non-work day looks back further; two successive holidays pass the test through the first); `payroll.regular_holiday_prior_workday` applies it to the daily-paid wage and `holiday.prior_day_present` to the double holiday’s second day.

wages.authority: Applied 2026-09-18 (2): the wage orders state a daily rate; `by_region` carries it × 313/12 and `wages.scale` restates the floor on the person’s own factor — 365/12 for the monthly-paid, 261/12 on a five-day week, 313/12 on a six-day one — and the apprentice’s 75% (RA 6727; Labor Code arts.61, 75). Applied 2026-09-19 (3): Wage Order No. IVA-22 (effective 5 Oct 2025; nwpc.dole.gov.ph/region-iva): non-agriculture ₱600 in the Extended Metropolitan Area and the component cities (`IV-A`), ₱550 in 1st-class municipalities, ₱510 in reclassified 1st-class and 2nd–5th-class municipalities, the last two stepping to ₱550 and ₱525 on 1 April 2026 — the version from that date carries the second tranche. Each figure is the daily rate × 313 ÷ 12. Applied 2026-09-23 (audit): sector floors beside the area ones, for an establishment whose `company.region` names its sector — `NCR-AGRI-SMALL` is NCR agriculture, service/retail of 15 workers or fewer and manufacturing under 10 (₱658 under NCR-26, ₱718 under NCR-28; nwpc.dole.gov.ph/ncr/); `IV-A-RETAIL-SMALL` is IV-A retail/service of 10 workers or fewer (₱485 under IVA-22 from 5 Oct 2025, ₱508 from 1 Apr 2026; nwpc.dole.gov.ph/region-iva/). Each × 313 ÷ 12. The RA 9504 minimum-wage-earner test reads the same floor, so an employee of such an establishment above the sector floor is withheld on. Applied 2026-09-23 (round 2): RA 10361 (Batas Kasambahay) s.24: a domestic worker’s floor is the regional board’s domestic-worker wage order, a monthly figure, never the establishment order — `by_employment_type.DOMESTIC`, held on its own (scale 1). NCR only, from the wage orders themselves: NCR-DW-05 ₱7,000 a month from 4 January 2025, and NCR-DW-06 (approved 15 January 2026, published 22 January, effective 7 February 2026; nwpc.dole.gov.ph/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/Wage-Order-No.-NCR-DW-06.pdf) ₱7,800 — from the version of 7 February 2026; this version, which closes before it, states ₱7,000. Other regions’ domestic orders are not transcribed.

sources.instructions:
Sources are the primary instrument first — the statute or regulation in the national law database, the gazette, or the table the authority itself publishes — one page per fact the version seals, never a news article or a commentary. A historical version lists the instruments in force on its own effective date. Where the primary host refuses the reader (sso.agc.gov.sg, officialgazette.gov.ph, peraturan.bpk.go.id, kwsp.gov.my, hrdcorp.gov.my answer 403 to Norbital-Public-Page-Reader) the authority’s own published table is listed instead, or the Wayback Machine’s dated copy of the authority’s own page or PDF (web.archive.org/web/<timestamp>id_/<url>) — never a host the reader cannot open.
officialgazette.gov.ph — the Official Gazette: Republic Acts, proclamations, executive orders. A proclamation is /<yyyy>/<mm>/<dd>/proclamation-no-<n>-s-<year>/ (HTML, full text); /section/proclamations/ lists the newest first; /nationwide-holidays/<year>/ is the holiday calendar. lawphil.net mirrors the same texts and is corroboration only.
sss.gov.ph — /pay-contribution/ carries the contribution schedule (the 2025 table PDF under /wp-content/uploads/ is 6.3 MB, over the reader limit: read the HTML page); /sss-circulars/ lists circulars by year.
philhealth.gov.ph — /advisories/<year>/ lists advisories; each is /advisories/<year>/PA<year>-<nnnn>.pdf (small, text). /partners/employers/ContributionTable_v2.pdf is the premium table.
pagibigfund.gov.ph — Circular 460 at /document/pdf/circulars/provident/Circular No. 460 - Guidelines on the Pag-IBIG Fund… (1.9 MB, text): the 1%/2% tiers and the ₱10,000 fund salary cap.
bir.gov.ph — bir-cdn.bir.gov.ph/local/pdf/Annex E RR 11-2018.pdf is the withholding table (monthly and semi-monthly columns, 0.3 MB); revenue regulation digests are under bir-cdn.bir.gov.ph/BIR/pdf/.
nwpc.dole.gov.ph — regional wage orders: /ncr/, /region-iva/ (and the other regions); /bwc-handbook-workers-statutory-monetary-benefits/ is the DOLE Handbook (factors, premiums, 13th month).
pco.gov.ph answers 403 to the reader; use the Gazette.

Finding changes (read these before comparing, every run):
Wage orders: read https://nwpc.dole.gov.ph/feed/ (RSS) for new RTWPB orders, then open https://nwpc.dole.gov.ph/statistics/summary-of-latest-wage-orders-issued-by-the-regional-boards/ and follow its 'Download PDF' (Latest-Wage-Order-Matrix-<date>.pdf, a text PDF with issue/publication/effectivity per region). Effectivity is 15 days after publication when the matrix leaves it blank. The regional pages (/ncr/, /region-iva/ …) link the signed wage-order PDFs. These are scans with no text layer, so take the figures from the matrix. SSS: newest CI number on /sss-circulars/, and the rate table on /pay-contribution/. PhilHealth: /advisories/<YYYY>/ and /circulars/<YYYY>/; premium changes are 'Premium Contribution … for CY<YYYY>' advisories. BIR: every www.bir.gov.ph listing (RR, RMC, WithHoldingTax) is a client-rendered shell ('Loading…'), so it cannot be read. Discover RR/RMC numbers from a big-4 alert list (PwC PH Tax Alerts, SGV/EY Tax Bulletin), then open the PDF at https://bir-cdn.bir.gov.ph/BIR/pdf/RR%20No.%20<n>-<yyyy>.pdf. Holidays: lawphil proclamation index for discovery only (officialgazette.gov.ph returns 403). Pag-IBIG and DOLE/BWC labor advisories are bot-walled: use news only to discover, and do not cite them.

work_rules.authority: Labor Code of the Philippines (P.D. 442, as amended) Book III: art.82 (coverage), art.83 (eight-hour day), art.85 (meal period), art.86 (night shift differential), art.87 (overtime), art.91 (weekly rest day), art.93 (rest-day premium) and art.94 (holiday pay), with Proclamation No. 1006, s.2025 for the 2026 regular holidays and special (non-working) days. Applied 2026-09-18 (2): art.86 and Handbook ch.5: the night shift differential is 10% of the hour’s own rate, so 13 on a rest day or a special day, 20 on a regular holiday, 26 on a regular holiday falling on the rest day, 15 on a special day on the rest day, and on the overtime hours of each 12.5, 16.9, 26, 33.8 and 19.5 (`night_premium` adds as expressions over the day; the first eight night hours of a rest day or holiday are its ordinary ones). Handbook ch.2 §D–E: a monthly-paid employee — one "paid every day of the month, including unworked rest days, special days, and regular holidays", declared on the contract as `terms.paid_rest_days` (applied 2026-09-23, round 4: the payroll group is the employer’s own label and states no law) — is prorated and has an absence deducted on the 365 factor, 30.4167 a month (`proration_by`); the daily-paid keep 21.75 or 26.0833. Applied 2026-09-19 (2): The night-differential ladder reads the day type (`day_type`, which the holiday takes under `holiday_rest_precedence: PUBLIC_HOLIDAY`); `holiday.kind` is the published row’s kind (PUBLIC | SPECIAL | SUBSTITUTE), and a day-type literal against it never matched. Applied 2026-09-23 (PH audit): Handbook ch.2 §D, ch.3 §C, ch.4 §D state each day's pay as a total — a regular holiday worked 200%, a special day 130%, a rest day 130%, a regular holiday on the rest day 260%, a special day on the rest day 150%. The salary (261, 313 and 365 factors alike) and the daily-paid roster already pay a working holiday at 100%, so its first eight hours add the rest: 100% and 30% (`OT-2.0X`, `OT-1.3X`). The 365 factor (`terms.paid_rest_days`) also pays the rest day in the salary, so on it the rest-day rows add 30%, 160% and 50%; every other employee's rest day is unpaid and the rows carry the whole 130%, 260% and 150%. Hours beyond eight are paid by no base and keep their whole 169%, 260%, 338% and 195%. Applied 2026-09-23 (round 2): DOLE Handbook (2022) ch.2 §C: where two regular holidays fall on one day (a `DOUBLE_HOLIDAY` calendar row), the day is at least 200% of the daily wage unworked (`DOUBLE-HOLIDAY-UNWORKED`: a second day’s wage) and 300% worked (`OT-3.0X`: two more days on top of the day the wage pays); the guide computations (ch.4 §D) give 390% on a rest day (`OT-3.9X-REST`, 290% for the 365-factor employee, `terms.paid_rest_days`, whose salary pays the rest day), overtime 3 × 1.3 = 390% (`OT-3.9X`) and 3.9 × 1.3 = 507% on a rest day (`OT-5.07X-REST`), and night shift 10% of those rates (30, 39; overtime 39, 50.7). Ch.2 §D–E: an unworked regular holiday is paid only to an employee present, or on leave with pay, on the workday immediately preceding it (a rest or non-work day looks back further; two successive holidays pass the test through the first); `payroll.regular_holiday_prior_workday` applies it to the daily-paid wage and `holiday.prior_day_present` to the double holiday’s second day.

wages.authority: Applied 2026-09-18 (2): the wage orders state a daily rate; `by_region` carries it × 313/12 and `wages.scale` restates the floor on the person’s own factor — 365/12 for the monthly-paid, 261/12 on a five-day week, 313/12 on a six-day one — and the apprentice’s 75% (RA 6727; Labor Code arts.61, 75). Applied 2026-09-19 (3): Wage Order No. IVA-22 (effective 5 Oct 2025; nwpc.dole.gov.ph/region-iva): non-agriculture ₱600 in the Extended Metropolitan Area and the component cities (`IV-A`), ₱550 in 1st-class municipalities, ₱510 in reclassified 1st-class and 2nd–5th-class municipalities, the last two stepping to ₱550 and ₱525 on 1 April 2026 — the version from that date carries the second tranche. Each figure is the daily rate × 313 ÷ 12. Applied 2026-09-23 (audit): sector floors beside the area ones, for an establishment whose `company.region` names its sector — `NCR-AGRI-SMALL` is NCR agriculture, service/retail of 15 workers or fewer and manufacturing under 10 (₱658 under NCR-26, ₱718 under NCR-28; nwpc.dole.gov.ph/ncr/); `IV-A-RETAIL-SMALL` is IV-A retail/service of 10 workers or fewer (₱485 under IVA-22 from 5 Oct 2025, ₱508 from 1 Apr 2026; nwpc.dole.gov.ph/region-iva/). Each × 313 ÷ 12. The RA 9504 minimum-wage-earner test reads the same floor, so an employee of such an establishment above the sector floor is withheld on. Applied 2026-09-23 (round 2): RA 10361 (Batas Kasambahay) s.24: a domestic worker’s floor is the regional board’s domestic-worker wage order, a monthly figure, never the establishment order — `by_employment_type.DOMESTIC`, held on its own (scale 1). NCR only, from the wage orders themselves: NCR-DW-05 ₱7,000 a month from 4 January 2025, and NCR-DW-06 (approved 15 January 2026, published 22 January, effective 7 February 2026; nwpc.dole.gov.ph/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/Wage-Order-No.-NCR-DW-06.pdf) ₱7,800 — from the version of 7 February 2026; this version, which closes before it, states ₱7,000. Other regions’ domestic orders are not transcribed.

sources.instructions:
Sources are the primary instrument first — the statute or regulation in the national law database, the gazette, or the table the authority itself publishes — one page per fact the version seals, never a news article or a commentary. A historical version lists the instruments in force on its own effective date. Where the primary host refuses the reader (sso.agc.gov.sg, officialgazette.gov.ph, peraturan.bpk.go.id, kwsp.gov.my, hrdcorp.gov.my answer 403 to Norbital-Public-Page-Reader) the authority’s own published table is listed instead, or the Wayback Machine’s dated copy of the authority’s own page or PDF (web.archive.org/web/<timestamp>id_/<url>) — never a host the reader cannot open.
officialgazette.gov.ph — the Official Gazette: Republic Acts, proclamations, executive orders. A proclamation is /<yyyy>/<mm>/<dd>/proclamation-no-<n>-s-<year>/ (HTML, full text); /section/proclamations/ lists the newest first; /nationwide-holidays/<year>/ is the holiday calendar. lawphil.net mirrors the same texts and is corroboration only.
sss.gov.ph — /pay-contribution/ carries the contribution schedule (the 2025 table PDF under /wp-content/uploads/ is 6.3 MB, over the reader limit: read the HTML page); /sss-circulars/ lists circulars by year.
philhealth.gov.ph — /advisories/<year>/ lists advisories; each is /advisories/<year>/PA<year>-<nnnn>.pdf (small, text). /partners/employers/ContributionTable_v2.pdf is the premium table.
pagibigfund.gov.ph — Circular 460 at /document/pdf/circulars/provident/Circular No. 460 - Guidelines on the Pag-IBIG Fund… (1.9 MB, text): the 1%/2% tiers and the ₱10,000 fund salary cap.
bir.gov.ph — bir-cdn.bir.gov.ph/local/pdf/Annex E RR 11-2018.pdf is the withholding table (monthly and semi-monthly columns, 0.3 MB); revenue regulation digests are under bir-cdn.bir.gov.ph/BIR/pdf/.
nwpc.dole.gov.ph — regional wage orders: /ncr/, /region-iva/ (and the other regions); /bwc-handbook-workers-statutory-monetary-benefits/ is the DOLE Handbook (factors, premiums, 13th month).
pco.gov.ph answers 403 to the reader; use the Gazette.

Finding changes (read these before comparing, every run):
Wage orders: read https://nwpc.dole.gov.ph/feed/ (RSS) for new RTWPB orders, then open https://nwpc.dole.gov.ph/statistics/summary-of-latest-wage-orders-issued-by-the-regional-boards/ and follow its 'Download PDF' (Latest-Wage-Order-Matrix-<date>.pdf, a text PDF with issue/publication/effectivity per region). Effectivity is 15 days after publication when the matrix leaves it blank. The regional pages (/ncr/, /region-iva/ …) link the signed wage-order PDFs. These are scans with no text layer, so take the figures from the matrix. SSS: newest CI number on /sss-circulars/, and the rate table on /pay-contribution/. PhilHealth: /advisories/<YYYY>/ and /circulars/<YYYY>/; premium changes are 'Premium Contribution … for CY<YYYY>' advisories. BIR: every www.bir.gov.ph listing (RR, RMC, WithHoldingTax) is a client-rendered shell ('Loading…'), so it cannot be read. Discover RR/RMC numbers from a big-4 alert list (PwC PH Tax Alerts, SGV/EY Tax Bulletin), then open the PDF at https://bir-cdn.bir.gov.ph/BIR/pdf/RR%20No.%20<n>-<yyyy>.pdf. Holidays: lawphil proclamation index for discovery only (officialgazette.gov.ph returns 403). Pag-IBIG and DOLE/BWC labor advisories are bot-walled: use news only to discover, and do not cite them.

work_rules.authority: Labor Code of the Philippines (P.D. 442, as amended) Book III: art.82 (coverage), art.83 (eight-hour day), art.85 (meal period), art.86 (night shift differential), art.87 (overtime), art.91 (weekly rest day), art.93 (rest-day premium) and art.94 (holiday pay), with Proclamation No. 1006, s.2025 for the 2026 regular holidays and special (non-working) days. Applied 2026-09-18 (2): art.86 and Handbook ch.5: the night shift differential is 10% of the hour’s own rate, so 13 on a rest day or a special day, 20 on a regular holiday, 26 on a regular holiday falling on the rest day, 15 on a special day on the rest day, and on the overtime hours of each 12.5, 16.9, 26, 33.8 and 19.5 (`night_premium` adds as expressions over the day; the first eight night hours of a rest day or holiday are its ordinary ones). Handbook ch.2 §D–E: a monthly-paid employee — one "paid every day of the month, including unworked rest days, special days, and regular holidays", declared on the contract as `terms.paid_rest_days` (applied 2026-09-23, round 4: the payroll group is the employer’s own label and states no law) — is prorated and has an absence deducted on the 365 factor, 30.4167 a month (`proration_by`); the daily-paid keep 21.75 or 26.0833. Applied 2026-09-19 (2): The night-differential ladder reads the day type (`day_type`, which the holiday takes under `holiday_rest_precedence: PUBLIC_HOLIDAY`); `holiday.kind` is the published row’s kind (PUBLIC | SPECIAL | SUBSTITUTE), and a day-type literal against it never matched. Applied 2026-09-23 (PH audit): Handbook ch.2 §D, ch.3 §C, ch.4 §D state each day's pay as a total — a regular holiday worked 200%, a special day 130%, a rest day 130%, a regular holiday on the rest day 260%, a special day on the rest day 150%. The salary (261, 313 and 365 factors alike) and the daily-paid roster already pay a working holiday at 100%, so its first eight hours add the rest: 100% and 30% (`OT-2.0X`, `OT-1.3X`). The 365 factor (`terms.paid_rest_days`) also pays the rest day in the salary, so on it the rest-day rows add 30%, 160% and 50%; every other employee's rest day is unpaid and the rows carry the whole 130%, 260% and 150%. Hours beyond eight are paid by no base and keep their whole 169%, 260%, 338% and 195%. Applied 2026-09-23 (round 2): DOLE Handbook (2022) ch.2 §C: where two regular holidays fall on one day (a `DOUBLE_HOLIDAY` calendar row), the day is at least 200% of the daily wage unworked (`DOUBLE-HOLIDAY-UNWORKED`: a second day’s wage) and 300% worked (`OT-3.0X`: two more days on top of the day the wage pays); the guide computations (ch.4 §D) give 390% on a rest day (`OT-3.9X-REST`, 290% for the 365-factor employee, `terms.paid_rest_days`, whose salary pays the rest day), overtime 3 × 1.3 = 390% (`OT-3.9X`) and 3.9 × 1.3 = 507% on a rest day (`OT-5.07X-REST`), and night shift 10% of those rates (30, 39; overtime 39, 50.7). Ch.2 §D–E: an unworked regular holiday is paid only to an employee present, or on leave with pay, on the workday immediately preceding it (a rest or non-work day looks back further; two successive holidays pass the test through the first); `payroll.regular_holiday_prior_workday` applies it to the daily-paid wage and `holiday.prior_day_present` to the double holiday’s second day.

wages.authority: Applied 2026-09-18 (2): the wage orders state a daily rate; `by_region` carries it × 313/12 and `wages.scale` restates the floor on the person’s own factor — 365/12 for the monthly-paid, 261/12 on a five-day week, 313/12 on a six-day one — and the apprentice’s 75% (RA 6727; Labor Code arts.61, 75). Applied 2026-09-19 (3): Wage Order No. IVA-22 (effective 5 Oct 2025; nwpc.dole.gov.ph/region-iva): non-agriculture ₱600 in the Extended Metropolitan Area and the component cities (`IV-A`), ₱550 in 1st-class municipalities, ₱510 in reclassified 1st-class and 2nd–5th-class municipalities, the last two stepping to ₱550 and ₱525 on 1 April 2026 — the version from that date carries the second tranche. Each figure is the daily rate × 313 ÷ 12. Applied 2026-09-23 (audit): sector floors beside the area ones, for an establishment whose `company.region` names its sector — `NCR-AGRI-SMALL` is NCR agriculture, service/retail of 15 workers or fewer and manufacturing under 10 (₱658 under NCR-26, ₱718 under NCR-28; nwpc.dole.gov.ph/ncr/); `IV-A-RETAIL-SMALL` is IV-A retail/service of 10 workers or fewer (₱485 under IVA-22 from 5 Oct 2025, ₱508 from 1 Apr 2026; nwpc.dole.gov.ph/region-iva/). Each × 313 ÷ 12. The RA 9504 minimum-wage-earner test reads the same floor, so an employee of such an establishment above the sector floor is withheld on. Applied 2026-09-23 (round 2): RA 10361 (Batas Kasambahay) s.24: a domestic worker’s floor is the regional board’s domestic-worker wage order, a monthly figure, never the establishment order — `by_employment_type.DOMESTIC`, held on its own (scale 1). NCR only, from the wage orders themselves: NCR-DW-05 ₱7,000 a month from 4 January 2025, and NCR-DW-06 (approved 15 January 2026, published 22 January, effective 7 February 2026; nwpc.dole.gov.ph/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/Wage-Order-No.-NCR-DW-06.pdf) ₱7,800 — this version states ₱7,800. Other regions’ domestic orders are not transcribed.

sources.instructions:
Sources are the primary instrument first — the statute or regulation in the national law database, the gazette, or the table the authority itself publishes — one page per fact the version seals, never a news article or a commentary. A historical version lists the instruments in force on its own effective date. Where the primary host refuses the reader (sso.agc.gov.sg, officialgazette.gov.ph, peraturan.bpk.go.id, kwsp.gov.my, hrdcorp.gov.my answer 403 to Norbital-Public-Page-Reader) the authority’s own published table is listed instead, or the Wayback Machine’s dated copy of the authority’s own page or PDF (web.archive.org/web/<timestamp>id_/<url>) — never a host the reader cannot open.
officialgazette.gov.ph — the Official Gazette: Republic Acts, proclamations, executive orders. A proclamation is /<yyyy>/<mm>/<dd>/proclamation-no-<n>-s-<year>/ (HTML, full text); /section/proclamations/ lists the newest first; /nationwide-holidays/<year>/ is the holiday calendar. lawphil.net mirrors the same texts and is corroboration only.
sss.gov.ph — /pay-contribution/ carries the contribution schedule (the 2025 table PDF under /wp-content/uploads/ is 6.3 MB, over the reader limit: read the HTML page); /sss-circulars/ lists circulars by year.
philhealth.gov.ph — /advisories/<year>/ lists advisories; each is /advisories/<year>/PA<year>-<nnnn>.pdf (small, text). /partners/employers/ContributionTable_v2.pdf is the premium table.
pagibigfund.gov.ph — Circular 460 at /document/pdf/circulars/provident/Circular No. 460 - Guidelines on the Pag-IBIG Fund… (1.9 MB, text): the 1%/2% tiers and the ₱10,000 fund salary cap.
bir.gov.ph — bir-cdn.bir.gov.ph/local/pdf/Annex E RR 11-2018.pdf is the withholding table (monthly and semi-monthly columns, 0.3 MB); revenue regulation digests are under bir-cdn.bir.gov.ph/BIR/pdf/.
nwpc.dole.gov.ph — regional wage orders: /ncr/, /region-iva/ (and the other regions); /bwc-handbook-workers-statutory-monetary-benefits/ is the DOLE Handbook (factors, premiums, 13th month).
pco.gov.ph answers 403 to the reader; use the Gazette.

Finding changes (read these before comparing, every run):
Wage orders: read https://nwpc.dole.gov.ph/feed/ (RSS) for new RTWPB orders, then open https://nwpc.dole.gov.ph/statistics/summary-of-latest-wage-orders-issued-by-the-regional-boards/ and follow its 'Download PDF' (Latest-Wage-Order-Matrix-<date>.pdf, a text PDF with issue/publication/effectivity per region). Effectivity is 15 days after publication when the matrix leaves it blank. The regional pages (/ncr/, /region-iva/ …) link the signed wage-order PDFs. These are scans with no text layer, so take the figures from the matrix. SSS: newest CI number on /sss-circulars/, and the rate table on /pay-contribution/. PhilHealth: /advisories/<YYYY>/ and /circulars/<YYYY>/; premium changes are 'Premium Contribution … for CY<YYYY>' advisories. BIR: every www.bir.gov.ph listing (RR, RMC, WithHoldingTax) is a client-rendered shell ('Loading…'), so it cannot be read. Discover RR/RMC numbers from a big-4 alert list (PwC PH Tax Alerts, SGV/EY Tax Bulletin), then open the PDF at https://bir-cdn.bir.gov.ph/BIR/pdf/RR%20No.%20<n>-<yyyy>.pdf. Holidays: lawphil proclamation index for discovery only (officialgazette.gov.ph returns 403). Pag-IBIG and DOLE/BWC labor advisories are bot-walled: use news only to discover, and do not cite them.

work_rules.authority: Labor Code of the Philippines (P.D. 442, as amended) Book III: art.82 (coverage), art.83 (eight-hour day), art.85 (meal period), art.86 (night shift differential), art.87 (overtime), art.91 (weekly rest day), art.93 (rest-day premium) and art.94 (holiday pay), with Proclamation No. 1006, s.2025 for the 2026 regular holidays and special (non-working) days. Applied 2026-09-18 (2): art.86 and Handbook ch.5: the night shift differential is 10% of the hour’s own rate, so 13 on a rest day or a special day, 20 on a regular holiday, 26 on a regular holiday falling on the rest day, 15 on a special day on the rest day, and on the overtime hours of each 12.5, 16.9, 26, 33.8 and 19.5 (`night_premium` adds as expressions over the day; the first eight night hours of a rest day or holiday are its ordinary ones). Handbook ch.2 §D–E: a monthly-paid employee — one "paid every day of the month, including unworked rest days, special days, and regular holidays", declared on the contract as `terms.paid_rest_days` (applied 2026-09-23, round 4: the payroll group is the employer’s own label and states no law) — is prorated and has an absence deducted on the 365 factor, 30.4167 a month (`proration_by`); the daily-paid keep 21.75 or 26.0833. Applied 2026-09-19 (2): The night-differential ladder reads the day type (`day_type`, which the holiday takes under `holiday_rest_precedence: PUBLIC_HOLIDAY`); `holiday.kind` is the published row’s kind (PUBLIC | SPECIAL | SUBSTITUTE), and a day-type literal against it never matched. Applied 2026-09-23 (PH audit): Handbook ch.2 §D, ch.3 §C, ch.4 §D state each day's pay as a total — a regular holiday worked 200%, a special day 130%, a rest day 130%, a regular holiday on the rest day 260%, a special day on the rest day 150%. The salary (261, 313 and 365 factors alike) and the daily-paid roster already pay a working holiday at 100%, so its first eight hours add the rest: 100% and 30% (`OT-2.0X`, `OT-1.3X`). The 365 factor (`terms.paid_rest_days`) also pays the rest day in the salary, so on it the rest-day rows add 30%, 160% and 50%; every other employee's rest day is unpaid and the rows carry the whole 130%, 260% and 150%. Hours beyond eight are paid by no base and keep their whole 169%, 260%, 338% and 195%. Applied 2026-09-23 (round 2): DOLE Handbook (2022) ch.2 §C: where two regular holidays fall on one day (a `DOUBLE_HOLIDAY` calendar row), the day is at least 200% of the daily wage unworked (`DOUBLE-HOLIDAY-UNWORKED`: a second day’s wage) and 300% worked (`OT-3.0X`: two more days on top of the day the wage pays); the guide computations (ch.4 §D) give 390% on a rest day (`OT-3.9X-REST`, 290% for the 365-factor employee, `terms.paid_rest_days`, whose salary pays the rest day), overtime 3 × 1.3 = 390% (`OT-3.9X`) and 3.9 × 1.3 = 507% on a rest day (`OT-5.07X-REST`), and night shift 10% of those rates (30, 39; overtime 39, 50.7). Ch.2 §D–E: an unworked regular holiday is paid only to an employee present, or on leave with pay, on the workday immediately preceding it (a rest or non-work day looks back further; two successive holidays pass the test through the first); `payroll.regular_holiday_prior_workday` applies it to the daily-paid wage and `holiday.prior_day_present` to the double holiday’s second day.

wages.authority: Applied 2026-09-18 (2): the wage orders state a daily rate; `by_region` carries it × 313/12 and `wages.scale` restates the floor on the person’s own factor — 365/12 for the monthly-paid, 261/12 on a five-day week, 313/12 on a six-day one — and the apprentice’s 75% (RA 6727; Labor Code arts.61, 75). Applied 2026-09-19 (3): Wage Order No. IVA-22 (effective 5 Oct 2025; nwpc.dole.gov.ph/region-iva): non-agriculture ₱600 in the Extended Metropolitan Area and the component cities (`IV-A`), ₱550 in 1st-class municipalities, ₱510 in reclassified 1st-class and 2nd–5th-class municipalities, the last two stepping to ₱550 and ₱525 on 1 April 2026 — the version from that date carries the second tranche. Each × 313 ÷ 12. The RA 9504 minimum-wage-earner test reads the same floor, so an employee of such an establishment above the sector floor is withheld on. Applied 2026-09-23 (round 2): RA 10361 (Batas Kasambahay) s.24: a domestic worker’s floor is the regional board’s domestic-worker wage order, a monthly figure, never the establishment order — `by_employment_type.DOMESTIC`, held on its own (scale 1). sources.instructions:
Sources are the primary instrument first — the statute or regulation in the national law database, the gazette, or the table the authority itself publishes — one page per fact the version seals, never a news article or a commentary. A historical version lists the instruments in force on its own effective date. Where the primary host refuses the reader (sso.agc.gov.sg, officialgazette.gov.ph, peraturan.bpk.go.id, kwsp.gov.my, hrdcorp.gov.my answer 403 to Norbital-Public-Page-Reader) the authority’s own published table is listed instead, or the Wayback Machine’s dated copy of the authority’s own page or PDF (web.archive.org/web/<timestamp>id_/<url>) — never a host the reader cannot open.
officialgazette.gov.ph — the Official Gazette: Republic Acts, proclamations, executive orders. A proclamation is /<yyyy>/<mm>/<dd>/proclamation-no-<n>-s-<year>/ (HTML, full text); /section/proclamations/ lists the newest first; /nationwide-holidays/<year>/ is the holiday calendar. lawphil.net mirrors the same texts and is corroboration only.
sss.gov.ph — /pay-contribution/ carries the contribution schedule (the 2025 table PDF under /wp-content/uploads/ is 6.3 MB, over the reader limit: read the HTML page); /sss-circulars/ lists circulars by year.
philhealth.gov.ph — /advisories/<year>/ lists advisories; each is /advisories/<year>/PA<year>-<nnnn>.pdf (small, text). /partners/employers/ContributionTable_v2.pdf is the premium table.
pagibigfund.gov.ph — Circular 460 at /document/pdf/circulars/provident/Circular No. 460 - Guidelines on the Pag-IBIG Fund… (1.9 MB, text): the 1%/2% tiers and the ₱10,000 fund salary cap.
bir.gov.ph — bir-cdn.bir.gov.ph/local/pdf/Annex E RR 11-2018.pdf is the withholding table (monthly and semi-monthly columns, 0.3 MB); revenue regulation digests are under bir-cdn.bir.gov.ph/BIR/pdf/.
nwpc.dole.gov.ph — regional wage orders: /ncr/, /region-iva/ (and the other regions); /bwc-handbook-workers-statutory-monetary-benefits/ is the DOLE Handbook (factors, premiums, 13th month).
pco.gov.ph answers 403 to the reader; use the Gazette.

Finding changes (read these before comparing, every run):
Wage orders: read https://nwpc.dole.gov.ph/feed/ (RSS) for new RTWPB orders, then open https://nwpc.dole.gov.ph/statistics/summary-of-latest-wage-orders-issued-by-the-regional-boards/ and follow its 'Download PDF' (Latest-Wage-Order-Matrix-<date>.pdf, a text PDF with issue/publication/effectivity per region). Effectivity is 15 days after publication when the matrix leaves it blank. The regional pages (/ncr/, /region-iva/ …) link the signed wage-order PDFs. These are scans with no text layer, so take the figures from the matrix. SSS: newest CI number on /sss-circulars/, and the rate table on /pay-contribution/. PhilHealth: /advisories/<YYYY>/ and /circulars/<YYYY>/; premium changes are 'Premium Contribution … for CY<YYYY>' advisories. BIR: every www.bir.gov.ph listing (RR, RMC, WithHoldingTax) is a client-rendered shell ('Loading…'), so it cannot be read. Discover RR/RMC numbers from a big-4 alert list (PwC PH Tax Alerts, SGV/EY Tax Bulletin), then open the PDF at https://bir-cdn.bir.gov.ph/BIR/pdf/RR%20No.%20<n>-<yyyy>.pdf. Holidays: lawphil proclamation index for discovery only (officialgazette.gov.ph returns 403). Pag-IBIG and DOLE/BWC labor advisories are bot-walled: use news only to discover, and do not cite them.

work_rules.authority: Labor Code of the Philippines (P.D. 442, as amended) Book III: art.82 (coverage), art.83 (eight-hour day), art.85 (meal period), art.86 (night shift differential), art.87 (overtime), art.91 (weekly rest day), art.93 (rest-day premium) and art.94 (holiday pay), with Proclamation No. 1006, s.2025 for the 2026 regular holidays and special (non-working) days. Applied 2026-09-18 (2): art.86 and Handbook ch.5: the night shift differential is 10% of the hour’s own rate, so 13 on a rest day or a special day, 20 on a regular holiday, 26 on a regular holiday falling on the rest day, 15 on a special day on the rest day, and on the overtime hours of each 12.5, 16.9, 26, 33.8 and 19.5 (`night_premium` adds as expressions over the day; the first eight night hours of a rest day or holiday are its ordinary ones). Handbook ch.2 §D–E: a monthly-paid employee — one "paid every day of the month, including unworked rest days, special days, and regular holidays", declared on the contract as `terms.paid_rest_days` (applied 2026-09-23, round 4: the payroll group is the employer’s own label and states no law) — is prorated and has an absence deducted on the 365 factor, 30.4167 a month (`proration_by`); the daily-paid keep 21.75 or 26.0833. Applied 2026-09-19 (2): The night-differential ladder reads the day type (`day_type`, which the holiday takes under `holiday_rest_precedence: PUBLIC_HOLIDAY`); `holiday.kind` is the published row’s kind (PUBLIC | SPECIAL | SUBSTITUTE), and a day-type literal against it never matched. Applied 2026-09-23 (PH audit): Handbook ch.2 §D, ch.3 §C, ch.4 §D state each day's pay as a total — a regular holiday worked 200%, a special day 130%, a rest day 130%, a regular holiday on the rest day 260%, a special day on the rest day 150%. The salary (261, 313 and 365 factors alike) and the daily-paid roster already pay a working holiday at 100%, so its first eight hours add the rest: 100% and 30% (`OT-2.0X`, `OT-1.3X`). The 365 factor (`terms.paid_rest_days`) also pays the rest day in the salary, so on it the rest-day rows add 30%, 160% and 50%; every other employee's rest day is unpaid and the rows carry the whole 130%, 260% and 150%. Hours beyond eight are paid by no base and keep their whole 169%, 260%, 338% and 195%. Applied 2026-09-23 (round 2): DOLE Handbook (2022) ch.2 §C: where two regular holidays fall on one day (a `DOUBLE_HOLIDAY` calendar row), the day is at least 200% of the daily wage unworked (`DOUBLE-HOLIDAY-UNWORKED`: a second day’s wage) and 300% worked (`OT-3.0X`: two more days on top of the day the wage pays); the guide computations (ch.4 §D) give 390% on a rest day (`OT-3.9X-REST`, 290% for the 365-factor employee, `terms.paid_rest_days`, whose salary pays the rest day), overtime 3 × 1.3 = 390% (`OT-3.9X`) and 3.9 × 1.3 = 507% on a rest day (`OT-5.07X-REST`), and night shift 10% of those rates (30, 39; overtime 39, 50.7). Ch.2 §D–E: an unworked regular holiday is paid only to an employee present, or on leave with pay, on the workday immediately preceding it (a rest or non-work day looks back further; two successive holidays pass the test through the first); `payroll.regular_holiday_prior_workday` applies it to the daily-paid wage and `holiday.prior_day_present` to the double holiday’s second day.

wages.authority: Applied 2026-09-18 (2): the wage orders state a daily rate; `by_region` carries it × 313/12 and `wages.scale` restates the floor on the person’s own factor — 365/12 for the monthly-paid, 261/12 on a five-day week, 313/12 on a six-day one — and the apprentice’s 75% (RA 6727; Labor Code arts.61, 75). Applied 2026-09-19 (3): Wage Order No. IVA-22 (effective 5 Oct 2025; nwpc.dole.gov.ph/region-iva): non-agriculture ₱600 in the Extended Metropolitan Area and the component cities (`IV-A`), ₱550 in 1st-class municipalities, ₱510 in reclassified 1st-class and 2nd–5th-class municipalities, the last two stepping to ₱550 and ₱525 on 1 April 2026 — the version from that date carries the second tranche. Applied 2026-09-23 (audit): sector floors beside the area ones, for an establishment whose `company.region` names its sector — `NCR-AGRI-SMALL` is NCR agriculture, service/retail of 15 workers or fewer and manufacturing under 10 (₱658 under NCR-26, ₱718 under NCR-28; nwpc.dole.gov.ph/ncr/); `IV-A-RETAIL-SMALL` is IV-A retail/service of 10 workers or fewer (₱485 under IVA-22 from 5 Oct 2025, ₱508 from 1 Apr 2026; nwpc.dole.gov.ph/region-iva/). Each × 313 ÷ 12. The RA 9504 minimum-wage-earner test reads the same floor, so an employee of such an establishment above the sector floor is withheld on. Applied 2026-09-23 (round 2): RA 10361 (Batas Kasambahay) s.24: a domestic worker’s floor is the regional board’s domestic-worker wage order, a monthly figure, never the establishment order — `by_employment_type.DOMESTIC`, held on its own (scale 1). NCR only, from the wage orders themselves: NCR-DW-05 ₱7,000 a month from 4 January 2025, and NCR-DW-06 (approved 15 January 2026, published 22 January, effective 7 February 2026; nwpc.dole.gov.ph/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/Wage-Order-No.-NCR-DW-06.pdf) ₱7,800 — this version states ₱7,800. sources.instructions:
Sources are the primary instrument first — the statute or regulation in the national law database, the gazette, or the table the authority itself publishes — one page per fact the version seals, never a news article or a commentary. A historical version lists the instruments in force on its own effective date. Where the primary host refuses the reader (sso.agc.gov.sg, officialgazette.gov.ph, peraturan.bpk.go.id, kwsp.gov.my, hrdcorp.gov.my answer 403 to Norbital-Public-Page-Reader) the authority’s own published table is listed instead, or the Wayback Machine’s dated copy of the authority’s own page or PDF (web.archive.org/web/<timestamp>id_/<url>) — never a host the reader cannot open.
officialgazette.gov.ph — the Official Gazette: Republic Acts, proclamations, executive orders. A proclamation is /<yyyy>/<mm>/<dd>/proclamation-no-<n>-s-<year>/ (HTML, full text); /section/proclamations/ lists the newest first; /nationwide-holidays/<year>/ is the holiday calendar. lawphil.net mirrors the same texts and is corroboration only.
sss.gov.ph — /pay-contribution/ carries the contribution schedule (the 2025 table PDF under /wp-content/uploads/ is 6.3 MB, over the reader limit: read the HTML page); /sss-circulars/ lists circulars by year.
philhealth.gov.ph — /advisories/<year>/ lists advisories; each is /advisories/<year>/PA<year>-<nnnn>.pdf (small, text). /partners/employers/ContributionTable_v2.pdf is the premium table.
pagibigfund.gov.ph — Circular 460 at /document/pdf/circulars/provident/Circular No. 460 - Guidelines on the Pag-IBIG Fund… (1.9 MB, text): the 1%/2% tiers and the ₱10,000 fund salary cap.
bir.gov.ph — bir-cdn.bir.gov.ph/local/pdf/Annex E RR 11-2018.pdf is the withholding table (monthly and semi-monthly columns, 0.3 MB); revenue regulation digests are under bir-cdn.bir.gov.ph/BIR/pdf/.
nwpc.dole.gov.ph — regional wage orders: /ncr/, /region-iva/ (and the other regions); /bwc-handbook-workers-statutory-monetary-benefits/ is the DOLE Handbook (factors, premiums, 13th month).
pco.gov.ph answers 403 to the reader; use the Gazette.

Finding changes (read these before comparing, every run):
Wage orders: read https://nwpc.dole.gov.ph/feed/ (RSS) for new RTWPB orders, then open https://nwpc.dole.gov.ph/statistics/summary-of-latest-wage-orders-issued-by-the-regional-boards/ and follow its 'Download PDF' (Latest-Wage-Order-Matrix-<date>.pdf, a text PDF with issue/publication/effectivity per region). Effectivity is 15 days after publication when the matrix leaves it blank. The regional pages (/ncr/, /region-iva/ …) link the signed wage-order PDFs. These are scans with no text layer, so take the figures from the matrix. SSS: newest CI number on /sss-circulars/, and the rate table on /pay-contribution/. PhilHealth: /advisories/<YYYY>/ and /circulars/<YYYY>/; premium changes are 'Premium Contribution … for CY<YYYY>' advisories. BIR: every www.bir.gov.ph listing (RR, RMC, WithHoldingTax) is a client-rendered shell ('Loading…'), so it cannot be read. Discover RR/RMC numbers from a big-4 alert list (PwC PH Tax Alerts, SGV/EY Tax Bulletin), then open the PDF at https://bir-cdn.bir.gov.ph/BIR/pdf/RR%20No.%20<n>-<yyyy>.pdf. Holidays: lawphil proclamation index for discovery only (officialgazette.gov.ph returns 403). Pag-IBIG and DOLE/BWC labor advisories are bot-walled: use news only to discover, and do not cite them.
Watch Wage Order No. NCR-27 (approved 23 June 2026: +₱60, then a second ₱25 tranche on 20 January 2027). NCR-28's recital says it never took effect under a status quo ante order, a TRO and a writ of preliminary injunction, and nwpc.dole.gov.ph/ncr/ marks it "subject to continuing litigation pending before RTC Pasig Branch 152 and RTC Navotas Branch 287". Read that page's NCR-27 notice on every check: if the courts lift the injunction, the 20 January 2027 tranche (and any restored NCR-27 rates) needs a new version from its effective date; NCR-28 (effective 26 September 2026) is not necessarily the last NCR order for that period.
